title: Parsons Awarded Contract Amendment Valued Up To $100M For Environmental Engineering Services
summary: Parsons Awarded Environmental Engineering contract to address complex environmental challenges with innovative remediation technologies.

5


minutes


## Key Takeaways


- Parsons was awarded a new $100 million ceiling-value amendment to an existing confidential contract to provide environmental engineering services.
- The scope includes sampling, waste characterization, remediation, and restoration to address complex contamination challenges.


CHANTILLY, Va. (November 12, 2026) – Parsons Corporation (NYSE: PSN) announced today that the company was selected to continue providing environmental engineering services for site remediation on the west coast of the United States. The amendment to an existing contract, with a ceiling value of $100 million, includes sampling, waste characterization, remediation and restoration.


“This award reflects the depth of our environmental engineering expertise and our proven ability to address the nation’s most complex environmental challenges,” said Mark Fialkowski, President of Infrastructure North America. “Our team applies innovative remediation technologies that protect communities, restore impacted environments, and support our client’s critical mission.”


Parsons has decades of experience delivering environmental solutions that help government and commercial clients address complex contamination challenges and protect community health. Our environmental engineering expertise includes initial investigation and planning through design, construction, regulatory compliance, monitoring, and site closure. By combining technical knowledge, proven field execution, and innovative remediation approaches, Parsons helps clients accelerate cleanup, reduce long-term environmental risk, and restore sites for safe and productive use. ****


To learn more about Parsons’ Environmental solutions, visit[https://www.parsons.com/environmental/](https://www.parsons.com/environmental/) .
